stem.en: Magnesium has two outer electrons. Oxygen has six. Kabir says magnesium oxide must be "one magnesium to three oxygens, because six divided by two is three". What is the recipe?

text.en: One magnesium to one oxygen. Magnesium gives two electrons, oxygen takes two, and both reach eight.

feedback.en: Oxygen does not need six electrons. It has six and needs two more to reach eight. Magnesium gives exactly two.
Each magnesium gives two, and one oxygen can only take two. A second magnesium would have nowhere to put its electrons.

text.en: It depends on how hot the flame is.

feedback.en: Recipes are set by valency, not by temperature. That was the lesson of the fixed recipe in Book I.

explanation.en: Count what is given and what is taken. Magnesium gives two. Oxygen takes two. One of each, and both outer shells are full.
